steps.title: Tithe map
steps.headline: c.1841 · Tithe map: Bute owns; John Williams occupies the holding
steps.short: About 1841: the tithe map lists Bute as owner, and John Williams as occupier.
steps.text: c.1841 · Tithe map: Bute owns; John Williams occupies the holding. VERIFIED · public copy. The tithe apportionment for Landough, Cogan and Leckwith lists the Bute estate as owner and John Williams as occupier of the Great House Farm holding.
steps.say: About eighteen forty-one: the tithe map lists Bute as owner, and John Williams as occupier.

steps.title: Root title splits: A / B
steps.headline: 1877 · Root title splits: Parcel A / Parcel B
steps.short: 1877: by a later statement (c.1974), the title splits. Bute sells Parcel A, the farmhouse and about ten acres, to Daniel Thomas, and keeps Parcel B. The farmer, John Williams, takes a tenancy from Thomas for quarrying. When quarrying ceases, Parcel A is to be his.
steps.text: 1877 · Root title splits: Parcel A / Parcel B. TESTIMONY · later statement (c.1974). A later statement (c.1974): the Bute Estate sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas and kept about 9 acres (Parcel B). John Williams, the farmer at Great House Farm, took a tenancy from Thomas for quarrying (the statement dates his lease 6 November 1877), and “when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to [John Williams]”. The 1877 instrument itself is not held (EV-0006).
steps.say: Eighteen seventy-seven: by a later statement, the title splits. Bute sells Parcel A, the farmhouse and about ten acres, to Daniel Thomas, and keeps Parcel B. The farmer, John Williams, takes a tenancy from Thomas for quarrying. When quarrying ceases, Parcel A is to be his.

steps.title: Bute tenancy: J. Williams
steps.headline: 1916 · Bute → John Williams (the son): yearly tenancy of the “whole farm”
steps.short: 1916: John Williams’s son, also named John Williams, has farmed Great House Farm since his father died in 1908. Bute grants him a yearly tenancy of the whole farm, Parcel A included. It is the last tenancy of Parcel A.
steps.text: 1916 · Bute → John Williams (the son): yearly tenancy of the “whole farm”. VERIFIED · judgment. John Williams died in 1908 and his son, also named John Williams, took over the farm (Barry Dock News, 23 Oct 1908, EV-0243; a later statement, c.1974). The Court of Appeal’s history describes a February 1916 yearly agricultural tenancy of the “whole farm”. It covered Parcel A: the last tenancy of Parcel A, whose occupiers the Williams family had been since 1667. The tenancy (EV-0014) is not held.

steps.title: Last rent paid; quarry ends
steps.headline: 1928 · Last rent paid; quarrying ends: Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s
steps.short: 1928: quarrying ends, and John Williams pays the last rent. His daughter, Mary (Nancy) Williams, born at the farm in 1913, later states that from then on he regarded the farm as his own: Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s.
steps.text: 1928 · Last rent paid; quarrying ends: Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s. TESTIMONY · Mary (Nancy) Williams. Mary (Nancy) Williams, John Williams’s daughter, was born at Great House Farm on 10 August 1913. Her statement (c.1974): the quarry machinery was removed in 1928 and her father made the last payment of rent, about £4 a year, to Alfred Thomas. “After this my father regarded the farm as his own.” Neither the 1877 deed nor the 1928 receipt is held.
steps.say: Nineteen twenty-eight: quarrying ends, and John Williams pays the last rent. His daughter, Mary Nancy Williams, born at the farm in nineteen thirteen, later stated that from then on, he regarded the farm as his own. Parcel A becomes the Williams family's.

steps.title: Mountjoy / Bute → WGR
steps.headline: 1938 · Mountjoy / Bute → Western Ground Rents Ltd (WGR)
steps.short: 1938: Mountjoy and Bute sell to Western Ground Rents. Which land that deed conveyed is the open question.
steps.text: 1938 · Mountjoy / Bute → Western Ground Rents Ltd (WGR). VERIFIED · deed copy + press. Sale announced 17 May 1938 and completed 23 Dec 1938. Later WGR deeds deduce title from “a Conveyance on sale dated 25th December 1938” (EV-0216, copy held). The 1938 deed and plan (EV-0019) are not held: exactly which land it conveyed is the open question.

steps.title: WGR plan: Parcel B only
steps.headline: 1939 · WGR → John Williams agreement: plan shows Parcel B only
steps.short: 1939: a Western Ground Rents agreement with John Williams. Its plan shows Parcel B only.
steps.text: 1939 · WGR → John Williams agreement: plan shows Parcel B only. VERIFIED · partly held. The May 1939 WGR agreement (Glamorgan Archives DBDT123/7) is a monthly let “as meadow or pasture land”; its plan shows the eastern fields (Parcel B) only.
steps.say: Nineteen thirty-nine: a Western Ground Rents agreement with John Williams. Its plan shows Parcel B only.

steps.title: Leckwith Woods gift
steps.headline: 1940–42 · WGR gives about 109 acres of Leckwith Woods to Cardiff Corporation
steps.short: 1940 to 42: Western Ground Rents gives Leckwith Woods, in Leckwith, to Cardiff Corporation.
steps.text: 1940–42 · WGR gives about 109 acres of Leckwith Woods to Cardiff Corporation. VERIFIED · secondary + press. Cardiff Parks: “The Council acquired a part of Leckwith Woods comprising some 109 acres as a gift from Western Ground Rents Ltd … offered and accepted in 1940, though the transfer of ownership was not formally completed until April 1942.” The deed carries a recreation-only covenant. The Western Mail (18 Mar 1955) says the woods were “bought by the corporation for a nominal sum in 1942”. Not seen: the 1942 deed and plan. The gift is of Leckwith Woods, which lies in Leckwith, not Llandough.
steps.say: Nineteen forty to forty-two: Western Ground Rents gives Leckwith Woods, in Leckwith, to Cardiff Corporation.

steps.title: Occupancy attempt rejected
steps.headline: 1949 · First attempt to make occupancy permissive, rejected
steps.short: 1949: John Williams’s tenancy is surrendered, and a new yearly tenancy goes to Frederick Buckler, who married Mary in 1936 and has run the farm since 1944. The written tenancy agreement that was intended never happens. The first attempt to make occupancy permissive, rejected.
steps.text: 1949 · First attempt to make occupancy permissive, rejected. VERIFIED · judgment. Frederick Buckler married Mary (Nancy) Williams in 1936 and, from 1944, ran the farm as manager for her father (her statement, c.1974). The Court of Appeal (1987) records that Mr Williams “fell into arrears with his rent in the mid-1930s and in the late 1940s. Because of that, agreement was reached for Mr Williams' tenancy to be surrendered and for a new yearly agricultural tenancy commencing at February 2 1949 to be granted to Mr Williams' son-in-law, Mr Frederick Buckler”. It records: “It was intended that Mr Frederick Buckler should have a written tenancy agreement, but this did not happen because Mr Frederick Buckler also failed to pay the rent.” The landlords’ agents wrote to their solicitors on 10 October 1952 “that they did not propose to proceed with the letting to Mr Frederick Buckler”. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s own statement (c.1974): “I have never had any doubt that I was entitled to do so nor have I ever paid rent to or acknowledged the title of anyone as landlord.” In November 1958 she told Glamorgan County Council’s planning committee that “the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents” (Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958, p.7; newspaper-archive OCR, page image not seen).
steps.say: Nineteen forty-nine: John Williams's tenancy is surrendered, and a new yearly tenancy goes to Frederick Buckler, who married Mary in nineteen thirty-six and has run the farm since nineteen forty-four. The written tenancy agreement that was intended never happens. The first attempt to make occupancy permissive, rejected.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Parcel B repossessed
steps.headline: 4 Jul 1955 · Possession of Parcel B, later misread and conflated with Parcel A; the woodland and the green were also seized, shortly after Mary returned from hospital with her leg amputated
steps.short: 4 July 1955: the possession order is enforced on all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden. Most likely that takes the woodland and the green, two parts of Parcel A, with Parcel B. Mary, just home from hospital after losing a leg, stays in the house.
steps.text: 4 Jul 1955 · Possession of Parcel B, later misread and conflated with Parcel A; the woodland and the green were also seized, shortly after Mary returned from hospital with her leg amputated. VERIFIED · judgment. The Court of Appeal records that WGR obtained a High Court possession order against Frederick Buckler “in respect of the whole of the farm”, and: “On July 4 1955 that possession order was enforced, and possession was taken in respect of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden.” It gives the reason: Mary “had recently come out of hospital after having had a leg amputated and was objecting very strongly to leaving the farmhouse.” What most likely happened: the order was made against Frederick, whose farm tenancy had ended, and the land WGR let is the eastern fields, Parcel B, on the 1939 WGR plan (EV-0023). On the 1947 Ordnance Survey (25-inch, Glamorgan sheet XLVII.6, revised 1941) the Ty-mawr house and yard sit between the wooded old limekiln and quarry ground to the north and the open ground to the south-east. The Three Parts of Parcel A page identifies those two areas as Parcel A’s woodland and green, with the farmhouse and garden as the third part. Taking “all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden” therefore took the woodland and the green along with Parcel B, and left Mary in the third part, the house. This station sits on Parcel B; the woodland and the green have their own lines. The order and execution return (EV-0032, EV-0034) are not held.
steps.say: 4 July nineteen fifty-five: the possession order is enforced on all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden. Most likely that takes the woodland and the green, two parts of Parcel A, with Parcel B. Mary, just home from hospital after losing a leg, stays in the house.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Leckwith Common inquiry
steps.headline: 7 May 1958 · Cardiff City Council’s Leckwith Common inquiry (Leckwith Common, not Great House Farm or Parcel A)
steps.short: 7 May 1958: at Cardiff’s Leckwith Common inquiry, Mary, reported under her married name as Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, does not oppose the plan, so long as it applies only to playing fields. It concerns Leckwith Common, not Parcel A.
steps.text: 7 May 1958 · Cardiff City Council’s Leckwith Common inquiry (Leckwith Common, not Great House Farm or Parcel A). VERIFIED · press (OCR). Mary appears in the press under her married name, Mrs Buckler. At the 6 May 1958 inquiry into Cardiff City Council’s plan to turn Leckwith Common into playing fields, the Western Mail (7 May 1958, p.7) reports: “Mrs. Mary Doreen Buckler, of Great House Farm, Llandough, said she did not oppose the proposal so long as it applied only to playing fields. About 130 years ago Lord Bute allowed her family ‘a slice of land’ which was now Leckwith Common.” The inquiry concerned Leckwith Common, not Great House Farm or Parcel A. Quoted from the newspaper archive’s OCR; page image not seen.
steps.say: 7 May nineteen fifty-eight: at Cardiff's Leckwith Common inquiry, Mary, reported under her married name as Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, does not oppose the plan, so long as it applies only to playing fields. It concerns Leckwith Common, not Parcel A.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Mary’s public objection
steps.headline: 19–20 Nov 1958 · Mary objects to Glamorgan County Council’s planning committee: her land “walked in and taken”
steps.short: 20 November 1958: Mary tells the county planning committee that the councils and Western Ground Rents “have walked in and taken” her family’s land: “a Welsh case of Crichel Down.”
steps.text: 19–20 Nov 1958 · Mary objects to Glamorgan County Council’s planning committee: her land “walked in and taken”. VERIFIED · press (OCR). The Western Mail (20 November 1958, p.7) reports the planning committee meeting of 19 November 1958: “Mrs. M D. Buckler was objecting to further industrial development in the vicinity of her farm, Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough.” Land farmed by her family since 1667 had been “wrongfully appropriated”. “This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down,” said Mrs. Buckler. “The Glamorgan County Council, Penarth Urban and Cardiff Rural Councils and Western Ground Rents have walked in and taken …” “Mrs. Buckler claimed that the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents.” Quoted from the newspaper archive’s OCR (search-result snippets; the sentence breaks off after “taken”); page image not seen.
steps.say: 20 November nineteen fifty-eight: Mary tells the county planning committee that the councils and Western Ground Rents have walked in and taken her family's land. In her words: a Welsh case of Crichel Down.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Green: occupancy attempt
steps.headline: 1958/9 · Green: attempt to make Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupancy permissive, refused
steps.short: 1958 to 59, the green: Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy, and she refuses it.
steps.text: 1958/9 · Green: attempt to make Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupancy permissive, refused. VERIFIED · judgment. The Court of Appeal records that by 1959 Mary asserted title to Great House Farm through her grandfather, John Williams, and: “She was offered a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden by Western Ground Rents but refused to accept it. She was also later offered, and refused, alternative accommodation.” The green lies south of the house and garden, now the Church View Close park, and was registered as village green VG41 on 16 June 1970. The offer and her reply (EV-0039) are not held.
steps.say: Nineteen fifty-eight to fifty-nine, the green: Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy, and she refuses it.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Woodland registration
steps.headline: 29 Mar 1961 · Woodland: deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City Corporation, about 12 years after the 1949 attempt
steps.short: 1961, the woodland: a deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick and Tile, and Cardiff City Corporation, about twelve years after 1949.
steps.text: 29 Mar 1961 · Woodland: deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City Corporation, about 12 years after the 1949 attempt. VERIFIED · register held. The woodland register WA735527 (copy held) lists “a Deed dated 29 March 1961 made between (1) Western Ground Rents Limited (2) The South Western Brick & Tile Company Limited and (3) Cardiff City Corporation”; the land tinted pink is subject to the rights in it, and the register notes “Copy filed under WA231076”. The deed and its plan (EV-0040) have not been inspected. The 1994 transfer is a separate, later event on this line.
steps.say: Nineteen sixty-one, the woodland: a deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick and Tile, and Cardiff City Corporation, about twelve years after nineteen forty-nine.

steps.title: Possession order
steps.headline: 11 Dec 1962 · Possession order: farmhouse and garden. The BP house line starts here
steps.short: 11 December 1962: a county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden. It is not enforced before 1974.
steps.text: 11 Dec 1962 · Possession order: farmhouse and garden. The BP house line starts here. VERIFIED · judgment. The Court of Appeal records that WGR sued Frederick and Mary Buckler in Cardiff County Court “for possession of the farmhouse and garden and mesne profits since 1955”, that “On December 11 1962 a possession order was made by Judge Temple Morris QC”, and that “nothing was done before 1974 to enforce the 1962 possession order”. The original order and plan (EV-0041) are not held.
steps.say: 11 December nineteen sixty-two: a county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden. It is not enforced before nineteen seventy-four.

steps.title: Weekly tenancy offer
steps.headline: 1965 · Further weekly tenancy offer; not signed, no rent paid
steps.short: 1965: Mary is offered a weekly tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid.
steps.text: 1965 · Further weekly tenancy offer; not signed, no rent paid. VERIFIED · judgment. Recorded in the Court of Appeal’s history: in March 1965 WGR’s agents offered Mrs Buckler a tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid.
steps.say: Nineteen sixty-five: Mary is offered a weekly tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid.

steps.short: 1967: Western Ground Rents and the City of Cardiff go to the Lands Tribunal. Which land it concerned has not been read.
steps.text: 1967 · Lands Tribunal: WGR v City of Cardiff. VERIFIED · catalogue only. A compulsory-purchase compensation case, catalogued at The National Archives. Which land it concerned has not been read.

steps.headline: 31 Dec 1969 · WGR → BP Pension Trust: BP takes WGR’s interest, including the 1962 order
steps.short: 31 December 1969: BP Pension Trust takes Western Ground Rents’ interest: Parcel B, and the 1962 order.
steps.text: 31 Dec 1969 · WGR → BP Pension Trust: BP takes WGR’s interest, including the 1962 order. VERIFIED · judgment. Conveyance recited as the root of BP’s title. The instrument and plan (EV-0043) are not held. The same conveyance carried Parcel B, so the station shows on both lines. In September 1974 BP applied for leave to enforce the 1962 order, so it held that order’s benefit.

steps.title: Village green VG41
steps.headline: 16 Jun 1970 · South-east ground registered as village green VG41 · about 11–12 yrs after the 1958/9 attempt
steps.short: 16 June 1970: the green is registered as village green VG41, about twelve years after the 1958 attempt.
steps.text: 16 Jun 1970 · South-east ground registered as village green VG41 · about 11–12 yrs after the 1958/9 attempt. UNVERIFIED. The date as recorded on the wiki. The application, map and ownership section of the VG41 file are not held; registration as a green does not by itself show who owns it. Llandough Community Council says it “owns and maintains the village green”.
steps.say: 16 June nineteen seventy: the green is registered as village green V G forty-one, about twelve years after the nineteen fifty-eight attempt.

steps.title: Ordnance Survey altered
steps.headline: 1971 · BP house: Ordnance Survey alteration
steps.short: 1971: an alteration of the Ordnance Survey. The source is pending.
steps.text: 1971 · BP house: Ordnance Survey alteration. SOURCE PENDING. An alteration to the Ordnance Survey’s “Ty-mawr” name for the farm in 1971; source pending until the 1971 OS sheet and its revision record are seen. On the earlier OS editions of 25-inch sheet XLVII.6 (1900, 1920 and 1947) the “Ty-mawr” name sits on the house parcel, Parcel A. The one 1971 record known on this line is BP Pension Trust’s 1971 abstract of title, known only from later recitals and not held (EV-0045).
steps.say: Nineteen seventy-one: an alteration of the Ordnance Survey. The source is pending.

steps.title: Attempt to extinguish fails
steps.headline: 1974 · BP house: BP’s attempt to extinguish Mary (Nancy) Williams’s ownership claim fails
steps.short: 1974: Mary opens the farmhouse to the public: “my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it.” BP’s possession action is adjourned, and never listed again. Its attempt to extinguish her ownership claim fails.
steps.text: 1974 · BP house: BP’s attempt to extinguish Mary (Nancy) Williams’s ownership claim fails. VERIFIED · press. UNVERIFIED · court papers. On 15 April 1974 Mary opened the farmhouse to the public and said: “my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it” (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974). BP brought a fresh county-court action for possession; on 3 July 1974 Mary pleaded that she owned the house parcel and relied on the Limitation Act 1939. The hearing was part-heard and adjourned, and was never listed again. BP also obtained leave on 19 Sep 1974 to enforce the 1962 order; Mary’s solicitors appealed because she had not been given notice, and the warrant was withdrawn on 31 Oct 1974. The court papers are not held (EV-0049).
steps.say: Nineteen seventy-four: Mary opens the farmhouse to the public: "my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it." B P's possession action is adjourned, and never listed again. Its attempt to extinguish her ownership claim fails.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: BP licence letters
steps.headline: 31 Oct 1974 · BP letters offer continued rent-free occupancy of the house
steps.short: 31 October 1974: BP’s letters offer Mary rent-free occupancy of the house. She never expressly accepts or rejects them.
steps.text: 31 Oct 1974 · BP letters offer continued rent-free occupancy of the house. VERIFIED · judgment. The letters were one-sided: the judgment records that Mrs Buckler “never expressly accepted or rejected the terms of the two letters”. In July 1974 her defence had asserted that the claim was barred by adverse possession. The Court of Appeal (1987) held: “whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse” (Dillon LJ).
steps.say: 31 October nineteen seventy-four: B P's letters offer Mary rent-free occupancy of the house. She never expressly accepts or rejects them.

steps.text: 23 Feb 1983 · BP Properties Ltd applies to register WA240304 (farmhouse and garden) · 8 yrs 4 mths after the 1974 letters. VERIFIED · HMLR. steps.text: 2 Feb 1987 · WA240304 merged into WA231076: the house branch joins Parcel B. VERIFIED · HMLR. Amalgamation recorded during the appeal; the application and plan (EV-0078) are not held.

steps.title: Court of Appeal
steps.headline: 31 Jul 1987 · Court of Appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2
steps.short: 31 July 1987: the Court of Appeal decides the farmhouse and garden only, and holds that the letters made Mary’s possession a licence. From here, no register shows the Williams title to Parcel A.
steps.text: 31 Jul 1987 · Court of Appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2. VERIFIED · judgment. The appeal concerned the farmhouse and garden only. The Court of Appeal (1987) held: “whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse”, so the adverse-possession claim to the farmhouse and garden failed. From here no register shows the Williams Parcel A title; the line runs on unregistered.
steps.say: 31 July nineteen eighty-seven: the Court of Appeal decides the farmhouse and garden only, and holds that the letters made Mary's possession a licence. From here, no register shows the Williams title to Parcel A.

steps.text: Nov–Dec 1988 · Eviction, then demolition (6 Dec 1988). VERIFIED · press. Possession was enforced at the end of November 1988 (forced entry reported for 30 Nov). BP demolished the farmhouse in the early hours of 6 December 1988.

steps.short: 10 November 1994: the woodland passes to Forest of Cardiff, a separate event from 1961.
steps.text: 10 Nov 1994 · Woodland changes hands: transfer to Forest of Cardiff, title WA735527 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation), not the 1961 registration. VERIFIED · register held. Transfer with plan to Forest of Cardiff, registered as WA735527. The current register copy is held (EV-0169); the 1994 transfer itself (EV-0136) is not. Forest of Cardiff’s accounts to 31 Mar 1995 show no land as an asset. The register (B1) enters Forest of Cardiff as proprietor on 25 Nov 1994. It recites a 23 May 1975 conveyance of part (“the land tinted blue … and other land”) from The British Petroleum Pension Trust to B.P. Properties Ltd, and notes copies of earlier deeds as “filed under WA231076”. It is a separate event from the 1961 registration.
steps.say: 10 November nineteen ninety-four: the woodland passes to Forest of Cardiff, a separate event from nineteen sixty-one.

steps.title: WA735527 part sold
steps.headline: 2005–06 · Part of WA735527 sold to Goldsworthy Homes: £20,000 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation)
steps.short: 2005: part of the woodland title is sold to Goldsworthy Homes.
steps.text: 2005–06 · Part of WA735527 sold to Goldsworthy Homes: £20,000 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation). VERIFIED · Companies House. A 2005 transfer excised land from WA735527 (EV-0139, not held); register entry A4 dated 22 Dec 2005 records the excised land being registered under a new title. Forest of Cardiff’s audited accounts to 30 Jun 2006 record “Sale of Land – Leckwith Road, Llandough £20,000”.
steps.say: Two thousand and five: part of the woodland title is sold to Goldsworthy Homes.

steps.title: Where each line stands
steps.headline: 2026 · Where each line stands today
steps.short: Today: Church View Close stands on the merged title. The woodland is Forest of Cardiff’s; the green is village green VG41. Parcel A’s Williams line runs on, unregistered.
steps.text: 2026 · Where each line stands today. VERIFIED · registers. Merged title WA231076 (house third + Parcel B): built over as Church View Close. Forest third: Forest of Cardiff, WA735527. Green third: village green VG41. Parcel A: the Williams line runs on, unregistered. HM Land Registry copies of the 1982–83 files are on order.
steps.say: Today: Church View Close stands on the merged title. The woodland is Forest of Cardiff's; the green is village green V G forty-one. Parcel A's Williams line runs on, unregistered.

steps.title: Parcel A: Williams title
steps.headline: 2026 · Parcel A: Williams title, not extinguished and not sold
steps.short: No deed of sale by Mary (Nancy) Williams is on file, and the 1987 appeal decided the farmhouse and garden only. The Williams title to Parcel A is not extinguished, and not sold.
steps.text: 2026 · Parcel A: Williams title, not extinguished and not sold. VERIFIED · judgment + registers. No deed of sale by Mary (Nancy) Williams is on file, and the 1987 appeal decided the farmhouse and garden only. Since 1987 no register has shown the Williams Parcel A title, about 38 years, while the three branch titles have been treated as valid. SOURCE PENDING A sale c.1965 reported in a cousin’s written account (held privately) is unidentified.
steps.say: No deed of sale by Mary Nancy Williams is on file, and the nineteen eighty-seven appeal decided the farmhouse and garden only. The Williams title to Parcel A is not extinguished, and not sold.

parcelA.note: Dotted outline: the whole of Parcel A from the 1877 split (Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement), kept on every later step. The woodland, green and house-and-yard labels appear at the step that first discusses each; the green is drawn as the lower third of Parcel A.

opening: This is the story of the true owners of Church View Close, Llandough, and why people incorrectly think it's Cardiff Forest, BP and Llandough Council.
framing: Station by station, it follows the title-chain map on the Legal Wiki’s home page, and shows why the Williams family’s title to Parcel A was never extinguished.
closing: Three attempts to make Mary’s occupancy look permissive were rejected. Each was followed by a registration of part of Parcel A in another name. And the Williams title to Parcel A was never extinguished: the line runs on.
